text:
Jorge (Acme Corp): Hey team — since ~10:12am UTC we started getting 429s from the /v1/generate endpoint. Spike is customer-visible. sample request-id: 0x7f9a2b3c4d. Any quick repro steps we should collect?
Sam S: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl you used and the response headers? also which api key/tenant id if you can share privately.
Jorge (Acme Corp): sending headers we captured: 
  x-request-id: 0x7f9a2b3c4d
  x-client-id: acme-web-123
  x-forwarded-for: 52.14.22.7
  status: 429
  x-rate-limit-limit: 120
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  x-rate-limit-reset: 165
  time: 2026-03-15T10:12:07Z
Sam S: perfect — can you also run this curl with an explicit X-Request-Id header so our logs match? 
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Request-Id: 0x7f9a2b3c4d-local" 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
Priya R: also please grab a HAR or use --trace with curl (or the browser network tab). If you can repro, run a small loop that hits the same endpoint and attach the timestamps.
Alex M: from the system side, can you confirm the tenant id and whether they have a Dedicated pool or hosted? if hosted, we need request ids + the precise minute window.
Jorge (Acme Corp): hosted. tenant acme-corp-prod. I'll attach HAR and raw response bodies to the ticket.
Telemetry Bot: [automated] Found 87 requests from tenant=acme-corp-prod between 2026-03-15T10:11:30Z and 2026-03-15T10:12:30Z that returned 429. Sample request-id: 0x7f9a2b3c4d. Burst pattern: 70% of traffic within 20s.
Sam S: Thanks — that matches a quota burst. Two useful artifacts to attach: 1) HAR or curl loop reproducer, 2) debug-bundle (logs + local client timeline). See: https://redwood.help/debug-bundle for instructions.
Priya R: For repro script, ask customer to run this locally (one-liner) to help us replicate rate-window behavior: 
  for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{http_connect}" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Request-Id: repro-$i" 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' & sleep 0.2; done
Alex M: If they can include response headers in the HAR we particularly need x-rate-limit-remaining and x-rate-limit-reset. If those are not present, send any X-Request-Id so we can pull server-side traces.
Jorge (Acme Corp): running now — will upload HAR + the curl output. I see repeated 429s after ~12 requests. x-rate-limit-reset ~45s each time.
Sam S: good — sending to eng for verification. @Alex M can you check server traces for request-ids starting with 0x7f9a2b3c4d?
Alex M: on it. pulling traces for that window... grabbing proxy logs + token usage. If we confirm a short burst above their configured quota we can propose smoothing (token-bucket tweaks) or brief uplift.
Telemetry Bot: [automated] Trace bundle created: trace-bundle-1908456789.zip (internal path /traces/1908456789).
Priya R: Once Jorge uploads the debug-bundle we can correlate client timeline to the server-side rate window and draft next steps. For now ask customer to include: exact clock time, sample request-ids, and a small reproducer (curl loop).
Jorge (Acme Corp): uploaded HAR + repro-output.txt + debug-bundle link to ticket. thanks all.
Sam S: thanks Jorge — we'll keep you posted. tagging @eng-oncall for follow-up if we need quota escalations or temporary bursts allowed. :thumbsup:
Alex M: initial look shows multiple concurrent connections from same client id; likely hitting hosted tenant quota. I'll propose a short quota bump while we advise client on client-side smoothing.
Priya R: closing loop: once eng confirms, we'll either SLO-exempt a short window or send exact quota window start/end to the customer + guidance.
Jorge (Acme Corp): appreciated.
